MachineWorks / field manual

Make the world work.

Place a component, wire it to a power source, and connect a switch, sensor, relay, or terminal to control its behavior. Select a device to change its output, motion, material, or custom parts.

Component → groundChoose a library card; click to place. R rotates placement.
V / G / P / C / TSelect / move / power wiring / signal wiring / test probe
Power or signal modeClick source, then target. Signal connections are directional.
Right-drag / middle-dragOrbit / pan. Alt + left-drag also orbits.
Wheel / F / HZoom / frame assembly / hide interface
E / D / DeleteInteract / duplicate / delete selected machine
Space / EscapePause simulation / cancel placement or wiring
Ctrl/Cmd Z / Shift ZUndo / redo an authoring change

Try this: select the control terminal and press E. The production line stops while its power supply remains online. The Airlock preset demonstrates a proximity sensor and OR relay; move the Probe near its sensor to open the door.

Real game logic, not engineering certification

Power is balanced per connected network in game-scale kW; storage uses kJ. The model has brownouts, stored energy, health, heat, cooling, trip latches, and one-tick-per-link signal propagation. It does not simulate AC phases, voltages, pressure, forces, real fluid transfer, or rigid-body physics. Conveyor cargo is a preview, not inventory transport.

Save / export / integrate

Save project preserves machines, parts, wiring, parameters, and a runtime snapshot as JSON. GLB exports the selected machine (or the whole assembly with nothing selected) as a static mesh snapshot. Animations and logic belong in the JSON and engine module. Edits autosave locally when browser storage is available.

The editor tries pinned Three.js r180 and falls back to a built-in WebGL2 renderer without a network. A reduced-detail software preview is used when WebGL2 is unavailable. The included module accepts the host's THREE and scene, and exposes update, serialize, load, on, and dispose. The existing WorldWorks host needs an explicit scene/lifecycle hook; this file does not silently patch it.

Workspace preferences

Render & simulation

The probe represents one game actor. In WorldWorks, feed the player's world position with engine.setProbe([x, y, z]).
